r7-classclosed.title: Is the layout-agnosticism class actually closed
r7-classclosed.imperative: Go through EVERY concrete mechanism description in the doc (S2, S3 worked example, S6, S7, S8, S9, S10, seam table, episodes/README.md) and for each ask: if Option A binds tomorrow, is the statement still true and does code written literally to this text still work. Trace concretely what g3 would implement for each retrieval primitive (fetch by id; enumerate non-retired; select by exact field restricted to ordinary set; enumerate neighbours) and whether binding Option A later requires touching that code or only writing adapters. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r7-classclosed.finding: DECISIVE QUESTION ANSWER: for the four g3 retrieval primitives named in the hunt (fetch by id, enumerate non-retired, select restricted to ordinary set, enumerate neighbours), the class IS closed -- traced each literally against the current text: fetch-by-id = resolve_episode_path(id) then read, no scan; enumerate-non-retired = iter_episode_ids(include_retired=False) then is_episode_in_ordinary_search() per id, exactly as S7's composition rule states; select/neighbours = same candidate set plus an extra predicate. Binding Option A later means writing 4 adapter bodies (a handful of lines each) at 4 already-named seams; none of S6/S7/S8's primitive descriptions change. No g3 primitive needs rewriting. S2 (id-sequence scan), S3 (worked example, now disclaimed), S9 (cross-worktree, now disclaimed), episodes/README.md (basename-only) all re-checked clean, no bare-path claim left unqualified. FAIL reason (a genuine but separate instance of the class, found by the same sweep): S5's worked amend-assertion write path ('the write path is one amend-assertion op... that changes exactly a4') and S10's g2-obligations bullet name NO seam for locating the target file before an amend write, unlike retire (apply_retirement) and fetch (resolve_episode_path). Unlike retire -- which always transitions FROM a known active state, so its Option-A source path is knowable without a check -- amend can target an ALREADY-RETIRED episode (S6 explicitly anticipates disputing/auditing assertions on a retired episode, since lifecycle-standing and retirement status are stated as independent dimensions), so under Option A the amend op genuinely cannot know in advance whether the target is under active/ or retired/ without the same two-directory resolution resolve_episode_path() already performs for reads. grep -n amend docs/EPISODE_STORE.md confirms zero co-occurrence with resolve_episode_path/apply_retirement anywhere in the document. If g2 is built literally to the current text (following the flat episodes/<id>.md pattern shown in every worked example) and Option A later binds, amending an already-retired episode's assertions breaks -- a real code change to g2's amend logic (adding a resolution step), not an adapter swap, because no seam is invoked to begin with. Mitigating factors, why this is not rated a blocker for THIS gate: (1) it is g2's write-path concern, not one of the four g3 primitives the hunt targeted; (2) the failure mode is a loud, self-diagnosing lookup failure (file not found), not round 1/2's silent-wrong-answer shape; (3) the fix is one sentence, symmetric to what rework 2 already did for retire and fetch-by-id; (4) g2 has its own review gate next. Secondary, minor finding: S8's bullet for select/neighbours ('both scan the same iter_episode_ids(include_retired=False) candidate set before applying their own field/key match -- identical composition to enumeration') is slightly ambiguous about whether the is_episode_in_ordinary_search() per-id filter is included; a careful reader resolves this correctly via the 'identical composition to enumeration' cross-reference and the primitive's own name ('restricted to the ordinary-search set'), so this is cosmetic, not blocking.

r8-seamcoherence.title: Seam coherence and non-redundancy
r8-seamcoherence.imperative: Check the four named seams (apply_retirement, is_episode_in_ordinary_search, iter_episode_ids, resolve_episode_path) plus the store-root seam for consistency with each other and with the prose: any overlap, gap, or contradiction; does the seam table match the prose; is it clear which seam a caller should use. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r8-seamcoherence.finding: Five seams (store root, apply_retirement, is_episode_in_ordinary_search, iter_episode_ids, resolve_episode_path) checked for overlap/gap/contradiction. Seam table (S7 lines 526-544) matches the prose exactly -- verified row by row against each seam's own paragraph. No contradiction found. Potential confusion point explicitly pre-empted by the text itself: is_episode_in_ordinary_search vs resolve_episode_path could look redundant (both touch active/retired under Option A) but S7 explicitly disambiguates them ('fetch-by-id needs no membership check at all -- but it does need its own path-resolution seam... which is a distinct concern from this seam, not a substitute for it'). iter_episode_ids vs is_episode_in_ordinary_search composition is explicit and load-bearing under Option B specifically (Option B's iter_episode_ids does NOT filter by include_retired on its own -- 'the retired/active split is left entirely to the per-id membership seam' -- so omitting the per-id filter after the scan is a correctness bug under Option B, masked as harmless under Option A; this is exactly the ambiguity noted as a minor/cosmetic finding under r7 for the select/neighbours bullet). No case found where a reasonable g2/g3 implementer would call the wrong seam; the one place the wrong choice (or no choice) is genuinely available is the amend-write gap already recorded under r7 (no seam is named at all for that path, so there is nothing to pick correctly or incorrectly).

r9-overcorrection.title: Over-correction check
r9-overcorrection.imperative: After three rounds of added structure, judge whether the doc is now harder to follow than the mechanism it specifies, whether any of the four seams is unnecessary, and whether it remains usable by a g2/g3 implementer. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r9-overcorrection.finding: All four seams are load-bearing, not speculative: each was added in direct response to a concretely identified gap (apply_retirement and is_episode_in_ordinary_search from rework 1; iter_episode_ids from round 2's named blocker; resolve_episode_path from the implementer's own sweep) -- none is generality invented ahead of a demonstrated need (see Fowler speculative-generality: absent). The document has grown to 653 lines and S7 alone is ~190 lines / 9 sub-topics -- flagged non-blocking under Fowler large-class -- but the S7-closing 'full seam set' table (5 rows: concern / seam / adapters) gives a genuine one-screen executive summary that keeps the doc navigable despite the prose density. A g2/g3 implementer who reads S7's table plus S8's primitive list has everything needed without re-reading all of S7's prose. Verdict: PASS with an observation (routed to g4, when S7 is next touched to record the bound choice) that S7 would benefit from a subsection split for readability -- not a blocker, and not evidence that any seam itself is unnecessary.
